subject: Air-gapped pilot & retention constraints — post-call action items
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Patel <sana.patel@medilabs.health>, Rohit Menon <rohit.menon@medilabs.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Air-gapped pilot & retention constraints — post-call action items

Hi Sana / Rohit —

Great talking earlier. Quick recap of what we captured on the call and a proposed short list of next steps so we can scope the air-gapped pilot and confirm retention/logging SLAs: 

Summary from call:
- Pilot scope: single-cluster Private deployment in customer-managed on-prem environment (air-gapped option for initial testing).
- Primary workloads: structured clinical note normalization and PII redaction pre-processing. No long-term model training in pilot.
- Data residency: all PHI/PII must remain on-prem, with no egress to hosted services.
- Retention: request is 30 days for request and application logs, 90 days for audit trails; security asks for immutable archival for 7 years (we flagged potential cost/feasibility gap).
- Logging: need structured access logs, redact user PII in telemetry, and provide an exportable audit bundle on-demand.

Action items I promised to follow up on:
1) Provide a concise list of deployment boundary patterns we support (VPC-only, air-gapped hostfile approach, controlled egress via bastion).
2) Confirm what telemetry/log types Redwood requires for operations vs. what can be turned off or scrubbed for the pilot.
3) Share a template data-flow diagram and a sample on-prem network checklist for customers running an isolated cluster.
4) Attachour SOC2 proof points and a short pilot runbook for review.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- By Tue 04/06: Redwood sends the deployment boundary doc + pilot runbook + data map template (deliverable: redwood_private_pilot_requirements.pdf, medilabs_data_map_v1.xlsx).
- By Thu 04/08: Medilabs returns a filled data map and any mandatory legal/regulatory redlines.
- Week of 04/12: Workshop with Security + Infra to validate air-gap feasibility and finalize retention windows.

Sana — a quick ask: can you confirm whether the 7-year archival requirement is strictly mandatory for the pilot or a longer-term production requirement? That will change the pilot design and storage options.

I attached the runbook and SOC2 proofpoints for reference.

Thanks,
Priyom
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0193
Attachments: redwood_private_pilot_requirements.pdf; SOC2-proofpoints-summary.pdf

From: Sana Patel <sana.patel@medilabs.health>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rohit Menon <rohit.menon@medilabs.health>, Medilabs Security <security@medilabs.health>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Air-gapped pilot & retention constraints — post-call action items

Thanks Priyom — helpful recap. A few clarifications from Security and Compliance after an internal review: 

- The 7-year immutable archival is a product requirement for any data touching PHI in production. For the pilot we can accept a reduced approach if we maintain demonstrable chain-of-custody and the ability to export an audit archive on-demand. 
- Retention windows: pilot target = 30 days request logs + 90 days audit trail backups (exportable weekly). That maps to our risk appetite for an experimental deployment.
- Telemetry: Security allows collection of operational metrics (CPU, GPU utilization, request latency). We must ensure request payloads are redacted before any telemetry leaves the cluster. No raw PHI may be included in telemetry.
- Network: Air-gapped is preferred; if full air-gap blocks necessary troubleshooting we will consider a one-way egress path to a customer-managed bastion (outbound-only) with strict allowlist.

We will complete the data map template — expect the initial return by Thu 04/08. For the workshop, include a short slide that maps Redwood log types to what Medilabs considers PHI vs non-PHI.

Sana Patel
Head of Compliance Programs | Medilabs Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Air-gapped pilot & retention constraints — internal: ask list for Security + Infra

Marissa / Aditya — looping you both in with Sana's reply (below). Quick questions for scoping: 

1) Data-flow template: I attached medilabs_data_map_v1.xlsx (sana asked for this back by Thu 04/08). Can we produce a filled example (anonymized) to accelerate their return?

2) Telemetry policy: Can we enumerate the precise telemetry fields Redwood writes today (e.g., request_id, token_count, latency, sampling of prompts) and call out which fields can be suppressed or scrubbed for the pilot? We need a short matrix: field -> can_scrub (yes/no) -> privacy impact.

3) Archival options: For the 7-year immutable archive ask, we probably cannot commit that for pilot infra on customer premises. Options: (A) recommend customer-managed WORM storage for production; (B) for pilot, provide an exportable weekly archive that Medilabs can copy to their long-term store. Need a one-paragraph recommendation that we can share with Sana.

Can you both review and I will consolidate answers into a single customer-facing note by EOD Thu 04/06.

—Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 7 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Air-gapped pilot & retention constraints — internal: ask list for Security + Infra

Thanks Priyom — quick status and next steps from our side: 

- Aditya: I reviewed the runbook and started a redline. The runbook already documents two standard patterns we can offer: fully air-gapped (no outbound) and bastion-outbound-only with allowlist. I'll attach a short one-page summary for the customer.

- Telemetry matrix: Aditya has produced the field matrix (see summary below). We will mark request payload sampling as "scrubbable"; request_id, latency, and token_count are required for debugging and will be emitted but with payload hashes (no raw text).

Telemetry summary (short):
- request_id: required, no PII, emitted (UUID)
- latency_ms: required, emitted
- token_count: required, emitted
- model_name: required, emitted
- prompt_sample: optional, can be disabled; if enabled it is redacted and hashed
- error_trace: required for debugging; scrub sensitive fields by default

- Archival recommendation (one-paragraph to share): For pilot we recommend providing weekly export bundles of immutable audit logs (signed/timestamped) that Medilabs can ingest to their long-term WORM storage. For production workloads that must meet a 7-year immutable retention, recommend customer-managed immutable storage (S3 Object Lock / on-prem WORM) behind their own KMS; Redwood can integrate export automation but cannot host long-lived PHI archives in hosted mode for air-gapped on-prem deployments.

Deliverables we will send by EOD Thu 04/07:
1) redwood_private_pilot_requirements.pdf (one-page deployment boundary options + runbook summary)
2) filled example medilabs_data_map_example.xlsx (anonymized)
3) telemetry_field_matrix.csv (field -> can_scrub -> notes)
4) a short slide mapping Redwood log categories to PHI vs non-PHI labels

Priyom — I can assemble the customer note and include the attachments. Once Sana confirms the pilot retention target (30/90 pilot) we'll lock the workshop date.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Attachments: medilabs_data_map_example.xlsx; telemetry_field_matrix.csv; redwood_private_pilot_requirements.pdf
